chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Walaad, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who kills himself intentionally is in the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally in it.' It was said to him: 'What is your view if he bequeaths a bequest, then kills himself immediately? Would his bequest be enforced?' He said: 'If he had bequeathed before an event occurred in himself, such as an injury or an action, from which he might die, his bequest is valid in the third. And if he had bequeathed after he had caused in himself an injury or an action, from which he might die, his bequest is not valid.'

key_terms.فِي الثُّلُثِ: in the third (part of the estate)

ai.seo_question: Does the will of a person who commits suicide remain valid according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential nuance of self-murder by linking the validity of the final will (wasiyyah) to the timing of the fatal act, distinguishing between premeditated bequest and impulsive self-harm. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating physical intent with legal consequences, ensuring that the one-third bequest is only honored if the individual was still in a state of soundness prior to the decisive injury.
